property_summary: For any admin caller creating a new EmergencyOracle via newEmergencyOracle(description), the created EmergencyOracle.owner() equals the admin caller (msg.sender); the mutant that passes address(this) as owner causes the created oracle's owner to differ (it becomes the C contract) for some admin callers.

For any admin caller address A and any description, after A calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the created EmergencyOracle's owner() equals A (the caller); the mutant that passes address(this) breaks this by making the owner be the C contract for some admin caller addresses.

For any admin caller and any description, after calling newEmergencyOracle(description) the deployed EmergencyOracle's owner is the calling admin (msg.sender); the mutant that passes address(this) instead makes the owner be the C contract for some admin callers, violating this rule.

For any admin caller addr and any description, after calling newEmergencyOracle the created EmergencyOracle's owner() equals the caller (msg.sender); the mutant that passes address(this) breaks this because the new oracle's owner becomes the C contract instead of the caller for some callers.

For any admin caller and any description, when they call newEmergencyOracle(...) the created EmergencyOracle's owner is a contract (non-zero code size) iff the call used address(this) as the owner parameter — the reference always sets the new oracle owner to the calling admin (an EOA) so the created oracle's owner is non-contract (code size 0), while the mutant that passes address(this) makes the created oracle owned by C which is a contract (non-zero code size) for some admin callers.

For any caller that is an admin, when they call newEmergencyOracle(description) the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's owner field equals the msg.sender (the admin); the mutant emits address(this) instead, so for some admin caller the stored/gettable owner in the event differs.

For any admin caller who creates a new EmergencyOracle via newEmergencyOracle(description), the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's first indexed parameter equals the caller (msg.sender) — the mutant instead emits address(this), so there exist admin callers for which the event owner differs.

For every admin caller, calling newEmergencyOracle(description) on the correct C emits NewEmergencyOracle with the first indexed parameter equal to the caller (msg.sender); the mutant instead emits address(this), so there exist admin callers for which the emitted owner differs.

For every admin caller and any description bytes, the NewEmergencyOracle event emitted by C records the caller (msg.sender) as the owner; the mutant emits address(this) instead, so there exist inputs (an admin caller and description) for which the emitted owner differs.

For any admin caller and any description, the EmergencyOracle contract created by C stores its owner as the msg.sender passed into its constructor (i.e., the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's first parameter equals the EmergencyOracle.owner()), whereas the mutant emits address(this) in the event causing mismatch between the emitted owner and the actual EmergencyOracle.owner() for some inputs.

After any successful call to newEmergencyOracle by an admin account, that account remains an admin (isAdmin[caller] == true) in the reference contract, but the mutant revokes admin rights (sets isAdmin[caller] = false) and thus can break this property for some inputs.

For any admin caller and any description, after calling newEmergencyOracle the caller remains an admin (isAdmin[caller] == true) in the reference; the mutant that sets isAdmin[msg.sender]=false can make the caller no longer an admin for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For any admin actor and any description, calling newEmergencyOracle must NOT change the isAdmin status of any other address (non-caller admins remain admins); the mutant revokes the caller's admin, which can be detected because creating a second oracle from a different admin should still be allowed and unaffected in the reference but can fail in the mutant when the caller was the only admin left.

For any admin caller and any description, after the caller creates a new EmergencyOracle the caller can still immediately create a second EmergencyOracle (i.e. newEmergencyOracle succeeds when invoked twice in a row by the same admin); the mutant that revokes isAdmin[msg.sender]=false after creation makes the second call revert for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any admin caller and any description, if an admin A calls newEmergencyOracle(description) and then a different address B (also an admin) calls newEmergencyOracle(description2), both calls succeed in the reference; the mutant that revokes isAdmin[msg.sender] may make the first caller lose admin rights and thus could prevent a subsequent call by that same address in some interleavings — we instead assert that creating an oracle by an admin does not affect the ability of a different admin to create an oracle immediately afterwards (i.e., second admin's call still succeeds), which the mutant can break when the only other admin is the caller and gets revoked.

For any admin caller and description, after calling newEmergencyOracle the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event reports the newly deployed EmergencyOracle's actual address (non-zero); the mutant emits a zero address (or wrong address) before constructing the oracle and so can produce address(0) in the event for some inputs.

For any admin caller and any description, after calling newEmergencyOracle the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event reports a non-zero oracle address (the reference always emits the actual new EmergencyOracle address != address(0)); the mutant can emit address(0) instead because it emits before construction.

For any admin caller and any description, after newEmergencyOracle returns the contract's NewEmergencyOracle event must report a non-zero newOracle address (the reference constructs the EmergencyOracle before emitting, mutant may emit address(0)); we test this by observing that calling newEmergencyOracle results in a deployed EmergencyOracle whose address is non-zero via reading c emitted oracle by constructing and then querying that deployed oracle's owner (callable view) — the reference allows interacting with the new oracle (owner() == admin) while the mutant's premature emit provides no accessible deployed oracle matching that owner for some fuzzed descriptions.

For any admin caller and description, after newEmergencyOracle returns there exists at least one contract at a non-zero address whose owner() == the admin (i.e., the newly created EmergencyOracle was actually deployed and assigned to the caller); the mutant can emit a zero/wrong address before construction and therefore may leave no deployed oracle owned by the admin, breaking this property for some inputs.
